meta.title: Weekend Adventures — Oct 31–Nov 1
meta.subtitle: From Crest View · ages 4 & 2
meta.intro: Ten family-friendly picks for Sat–Sun October 31–November 1, 2026 near Snoqualmie, for a 4-year-old and a 2-year-old. Drive times are from 6715 Crest View Ave SE.
meta.deep_pass_note: Research run Wed Oct 28: Halloween is Saturday and the weather looks dry and mostly sunny both days. It's the last weekend for the Halloween Train, Remlinger, Jubilee and Fall City Farms. Happiest Halloween on the Ridge is 6–8 PM Saturday, five minutes from home.
meta.signoff: Reply if you want a pure indoor Saturday plan or a Sunday outdoor loop.

weather.summary: Sunny morning, partly cloudy afternoon, dry (2–4% rain)
Cloudy morning, sunny afternoon, dry (1% rain)

ideas.name: Northwest Railway Museum Halloween Train (final weekend)
ideas.hook: Two-hour vintage train ride to the top of Snoqualmie Falls, with a 30-minute stop for cider, apple pressing, crafts and Eric Ode's music.
ideas.drive: ~10 min to Snoqualmie Depot; ~15–20 min to North Bend Depot
ideas.hours_detail: Sat Oct 31 and Sun Nov 1. Departs North Bend Depot 10:30, 12:30, 2:30; Snoqualmie Depot 11:00, 1:00, 3:00. Last weekend of the season.
ideas.why: Last weekend, and Saturday is Halloween itself. Close to home and rain or shine, only slightly spooky, and every child gets a small gift. The 10:30 North Bend or 11:00 Snoqualmie train is back before nap.
ideas.rain_backup: Runs rain or shine; both days look dry.
ideas.food_area: Downtown Snoqualmie (SQ Depot) or downtown North Bend (NB Depot)

restaurants.name: Copperstone Family Spaghetti (downtown Snoqualmie, near SQ Depot)
restaurants.known_for: Casual family Italian pasta/pizza.
restaurants.praise: Portions, kids’ options, and cozy booths.
restaurants.kid_note: Short walk from the Snoqualmie Depot; booths and kids' options.

restaurants.name: Snoqualmie Falls Brewery
restaurants.known_for: Small independent brewery since 1997 in historic downtown Snoqualmie, with a full kitchen and a kids' menu.
restaurants.kid_note: Kids' menu (grilled cheese, Uncrustables, mac & cheese bites). Sit-down only, no play area. Sat noon–9, Sun noon–8.

restaurants.name: Sigillo Cellars (Snoqualmie)
restaurants.known_for: Family-run winery tasting room in downtown Snoqualmie with a full food menu (salads, flatbreads, shareable plates) and non-alcoholic drinks.
restaurants.kid_note: Kids of any age welcome (they count toward the party size and stay seated with you). No play area. Sat noon–10, Sun noon–5.

restaurants.name: South Fork (if boarding in North Bend)
restaurants.known_for: Café, bar and beer garden off I-90 Exit 32 with a scratch kitchen, kids' menu, 20 PNW taps and espresso.
restaurants.kid_note: Kids' play area, covered sandbox and open fields; heated covered tent if it rains. Open Sat–Sun 8 AM–9 PM, weekend brunch until 1. Walk-ins only.

restaurants.name: Twede’s Cafe
restaurants.known_for: The Twin Peaks “Double R” diner for cherry pie, coffee, and huge breakfasts.
restaurants.praise: Massive portions, friendly staff, and the pie/coffee combo.
restaurants.kid_note: Booths + all-day breakfast make a messy post-falls rewind easy; pie doubles as the dessert backup.

restaurants.name: Snoqualmie Ice Cream (Historic Downtown SQ, near SQ Depot)
restaurants.known_for: Local scoop-shop flavors (German Chocolate Cake, Mukilteo Mudd, honey lavender) at 8102 Railroad Ave SE — rebuilt/reopened after the 2024 fire.
restaurants.praise: Rich creamy scoops, friendly service, and shaded outdoor tables.
restaurants.kid_note: Opens around noon on weekends; a costume-friendly treat after the Snoqualmie return.

restaurants.name: Friends & Co Ice Cream
restaurants.known_for: Creamy local scoops, seasonal flavors (lavender honey, mountain huckleberry), and a bright downtown shop.
restaurants.praise: Unique flavors, friendly staff, and indoor seating.
restaurants.kid_note: Indoor scoops if Scott's line is long or it's raining; Sat opens noon.

good_to_know.bring: Costumes encouraged for all ages. Tickets are needed for everyone 2 and up.
good_to_know.hours_note: Arrive at least 30 minutes before departure. This is the last weekend; Santa trains start later in the season.

ideas.name: Howl-O-Ween at Cougar Mountain Zoo
ideas.hook: Halloween day at the small hillside zoo: trick-or-treating from enclosure to enclosure, a pumpkin scavenger hunt, a costume contest and Halloween treats for the animals.
ideas.cost: Kids 2–12 free in costume; adults $18; under 3 free
ideas.hours_detail: Sat Oct 31 only, 9:30 AM–5 PM, regular zoo hours. 19525 SE 54th St, Issaquah.
ideas.why: Both kids get in free in costume, so it's mostly the adult tickets. The zoo is small and walkable, and the trick-or-treat route keeps a 2-year-old moving. A sunny Halloween morning is the best time to go.
ideas.rain_backup: Mostly outdoors; Saturday looks sunny and dry.

good_to_know.bring: Costumes (that's what makes the kids free) and a candy bag.
good_to_know.hours_note: Buying admission ahead is recommended. Children 15 and under must be with an adult.

restaurants.name: Levitate Gastropub
restaurants.known_for: Scratch-made modern American pub on Front St, open to all ages, with a kids' menu.
restaurants.kid_note: Weekend brunch 10–2 with Nutella or PB&J crêpes for kids. About a 3-minute walk from the hatchery.

restaurants.name: Formula Brewing
restaurants.known_for: Issaquah brewery with a taproom, beer garden and kitchen (pizza, wings, salads, pretzels).
restaurants.kid_note: Kids welcome inside and out (supervised). Open 11:30 daily; Sat to 10, Sun to 9. About 10 min from the farm.

restaurants.name: Flying Pie Pizzeria
restaurants.known_for: Locally owned pizzeria on Front St in downtown Issaquah.
restaurants.kid_note: Easy shared pies after the creek.

restaurants.name: Boehm’s Candies
restaurants.known_for: Issaquah chocolate and candy maker since 1942: hand-dipped chocolates, caramels and seasonal Halloween treats.
restaurants.kid_note: A short drive up Gilman Blvd for a Halloween treat on the way home.

ideas.name: KidsQuest Spooktacular: Haunted Hoedown
ideas.hook: Halloween day across the whole children's museum, with a rodeo theme: costume games, festive activities and the regular hands-on exhibits.
ideas.drive: ~30 min via I-90 W / I-405 N
ideas.cost: About $17 per person (listings vary $15–$18); under 1 and members free
ideas.hours_detail: Sat Oct 31 only, 9 AM–4 PM. 1116 108th Ave NE, Bellevue.
ideas.why: Indoors and made for kids up to about 10, so both kids can play at their own level. Costumes encouraged (cowboy and cowgirl fit the theme). A 9 or 9:30 entry gets you home for nap.

good_to_know.bring: Costumes. Eating is only allowed at the museum's snack spots.
good_to_know.hours_note: Reserve a time slot online; reservations are non-refundable and holiday days can fill up.

restaurants.name: Bellevue Brewing (Spring District)
restaurants.known_for: Spring District brewpub with upscale pub fare and a 2,500 sq ft outdoor beer garden.
restaurants.kid_note: Kid friendly: under-21s allowed in the restaurant and patio (not the bar). Opens 11:30; Sat to 10, Sun to 9. 4 hrs free garage parking.

restaurants.name: Din Tai Fung (Lincoln Square)
restaurants.known_for: Xiao long bao and Taiwanese-Chinese dumplings/noodles.
restaurants.praise: Consistent dumplings and efficient service.
restaurants.kid_note: Share noodles/buns; reserve or expect a wait — still worth it for a museum morning.

restaurants.name: Cielo Cocina Mexicana
restaurants.known_for: Made-in-house Mexican plates, chips/salsa, and a lively patio near downtown Bellevue.
restaurants.praise: Carne asada, generous portions, and staff who are warm with kids.
restaurants.kid_note: Family sit-down with shareable plates.

restaurants.name: Molly Moon’s Homemade Ice Cream (downtown Bellevue)
restaurants.known_for: Scratch-made scoops, seasonal flavors, and a pastry kitchen near Downtown Park / Inspiration Playground (steps from the museum orbit).
restaurants.praise: Chunky flavors, fresh cones, and friendly scoop staff.
restaurants.kid_note: Opens noon; a treat walk near Downtown Park.

ideas.name: Remlinger Farms Fall Harvest Pumpkin Festival (closing weekend)
ideas.hook: Big farm fun park: 70+ rides and attractions, steam train, hay ride to Pumpkin Village, corn maze and the U-pick field.
ideas.cost: $33.95 online / $34.95 gate (ages 2–64); under 2 free; pony rides $7
ideas.hours_detail: Fri Oct 30–Sun Nov 1, 10 AM–6 PM; last admission 5 PM. Sunday Nov 1 is the last day of the season. Costume contest on Halloween (Sat); start time posted at the gate that morning.
ideas.why: Closing weekend, with a costume contest on Halloween. Lots of rides for under-36" kids (Tiny Tots Train, Diggity Diggers, Mini Carousel, Bunny Hopper). The wristband allows re-entry, so you can go home for nap and come back after 3.
ideas.rain_backup: Mostly outdoors; both days look dry, but the fields are still muddy.
ideas.food_area: On the farm + Carnation town (Tolt Ave)

restaurants.name: Remlinger Brewery (Carnation)
restaurants.known_for: Beer brewed on the farm, cocktails and a full café menu.
restaurants.kid_note: All ages welcome; free parking. Taproom Fri–Sat noon–9, Sun noon–7.

restaurants.name: Remlinger festival treats
restaurants.known_for: Pumpkin-pie-spice donuts and caramel apples at the festival food stands.
restaurants.kid_note: At the festival food stands.

restaurants.name: Ixtapa
restaurants.known_for: Family Mexican plates and margaritas on Tolt Ave.
restaurants.praise: Friendly service, tortilla soup, and generous portions.
restaurants.kid_note: Warm indoor booths if the farm got muddy.

restaurants.name: Red Pepper Pizzeria and Pasta (Carnation Station)
restaurants.known_for: Pizza, pasta, and breadsticks.
restaurants.praise: Crust, service, and a casual local vibe.
restaurants.kid_note: Sit-down pasta when Blake’s counter feels too rushed.

restaurants.name: Blake’s Pizzeria & Ice Cream
restaurants.known_for: Giant slices, grinders, and ice cream scoops/shakes since the ’80s on Eugene St.
restaurants.praise: Fast counter service, big kid-friendly slices, and classic scoops.
restaurants.kid_note: Easiest town treat stop after the farm; one giant slice + a scoop often feeds a preschooler.

good_to_know.parking: Free on-site parking; arrive before 11 on Saturday for a short walk.
good_to_know.hours_note: Buy online: $1 less and Saturdays can sell out. Pony rides 11–4, check in by 3:30. Costume contest is Sat Oct 31.

ideas.name: Jubilee Farm Harvest Festival (last day Sat)
ideas.hook: Family farm festival: tractor and horse-drawn rides to the pumpkin patch, a small hay maze, animals, hot cider and a jug band on the porch.
ideas.drive: ~20–25 min via Fall City / W Snoqualmie River Rd
ideas.cost: Free admission and parking; pumpkins and pony rides ($9) extra
ideas.hours_detail: Sat Oct 31, 10 AM–5 PM. Last day of the festival.
ideas.why: Free and low-key. The hay maze is sized for little kids, and the free tractor or draft-horse wagon goes out to the patch. There's a pumpkin-washing station back at the barn.
ideas.rain_backup: Saturday looks dry. Pony rides are cancelled if it's too wet; horse team usually retires around 3.

restaurants.name: On-site hot spiced cider / barn snacks
restaurants.known_for: Cider-pressing vibes and fall snacks (farm stand).
restaurants.praise: ParentMap/farm copy highlight cider, animals, and porch music.
restaurants.kid_note: Easy snack right on the farm.

restaurants.name: Remlinger Brewery (Carnation)
restaurants.known_for: Beer brewed on the farm, cocktails and a full café menu.
restaurants.kid_note: All ages welcome; free parking. Taproom Fri–Sat noon–9, Sun noon–7.

restaurants.name: Ixtapa
restaurants.known_for: Family Mexican plates and margaritas on Tolt Ave.
restaurants.praise: Friendly service, tortilla soup, and generous portions.
restaurants.kid_note: Warm indoor booths if the farm got muddy.

restaurants.name: Red Pepper Pizzeria and Pasta (Carnation Station)
restaurants.known_for: Pizza, pasta, and breadsticks.
restaurants.praise: Crust, service, and a casual local vibe.
restaurants.kid_note: Sit-down pasta when Blake’s counter feels too rushed.

restaurants.name: Kelsey’s Koffee
restaurants.known_for: Coffee, pastries, and breakfast burritos in town.
restaurants.praise: Friendly service and dog-friendly seating.
restaurants.kid_note: Parent caffeine + pastry while littles decompress.

restaurants.name: Blake’s Pizzeria & Ice Cream
restaurants.known_for: Giant slices, grinders, and ice cream scoops/shakes since the ’80s on Eugene St.
restaurants.praise: Fast counter service, big kid-friendly slices, and classic scoops.
restaurants.kid_note: Easiest town treat stop after the farm; one giant slice + a scoop often feeds a preschooler.

good_to_know.hours_note: Last day is Sat Oct 31. Horse-drawn carriage often retires around 3 PM.

ideas.name: Fall City Farms pumpkin patch (last day Sat)
ideas.hook: Small farm pumpkin patch with farm animals, hot mini doughnuts and cider.
ideas.cost: Free to visit; pay for pumpkins and snacks
ideas.hours_detail: Sat Oct 31, 10 AM–6 PM. Last day of the season (closed Sunday Nov 1).
ideas.why: The closest pumpkin patch, on its last day. Short, simple outing: animals, a pumpkin each, hot mini doughnuts and cider. Works in the morning or after nap before the evening trick-or-treating.

restaurants.name: El Caporal
restaurants.known_for: Casual Mexican plates on Redmond–Fall City Rd.
restaurants.praise: Salsa, portions, and friendly service.
restaurants.kid_note: Open from 11 AM — realistic sit-down before nap, unlike the Roadhouse’s weekend 2 PM open.

restaurants.name: Small Fryes
restaurants.known_for: Burgers, fries and shakes with outdoor seating and a drive-thru.
restaurants.kid_note: Sat 11–9, Sun 11–8. Quick lunch before nap.

restaurants.name: South Fork (North Bend)
restaurants.known_for: Café, bar and beer garden off I-90 Exit 32 with a scratch kitchen, kids' menu, 20 PNW taps and espresso.
restaurants.kid_note: Kids' play area, covered sandbox and open fields; heated covered tent if it rains. Open Sat–Sun 8 AM–9 PM, weekend brunch until 1. Walk-ins only.

restaurants.name: Fall City Farms mini doughnuts & cider
restaurants.known_for: Hot mini doughnuts and cider at the farm.
restaurants.kid_note: On-site treat.

restaurants.name: MOOO! Ice Cream Shop
restaurants.known_for: House flavors, handmade waffle cones, and a bright kid-friendly shop on Preston–Fall City Rd.
restaurants.praise: Taste, friendly staff, and indoor/outdoor seating.
restaurants.kid_note: Sat opens noon; a good stop after the patch.

good_to_know.hours_note: Sat Oct 31 is the last day of the season.

ideas.name: Happiest Halloween on Snoqualmie Ridge
ideas.hook: Free Halloween-night trick-or-treating around the Ridge, with big costumed sets (Princess Castle, Pirate Ship), hot cider stands and indoor rooms at Church on the Ridge.
ideas.hours_detail: Sat Oct 31 only, 6–8 PM. Indoor rooms at Church on the Ridge, 35221 SE Douglas St; Princess Castle at 7328 SE Curtis Dr; Pirate Ship at 7233 Douglas Ave SE.
ideas.why: Our own neighborhood on Halloween night, built to be friendly rather than scary. The indoor Glo Party is for ages 2–5, so both kids fit. Do the castle and pirate ship, grab cider, and be home for bed.
ideas.rain_backup: Indoor rooms at the church if it gets cold; Saturday evening looks dry.

good_to_know.bring: Costumes, a treat bag and warm layers (it'll be in the 40s). A map of the stops is on the church's page.
good_to_know.hours_note: Starts at 6, a little later than our usual afternoon block.

restaurants.name: Frankie’s Pizza
restaurants.known_for: Custom thin-crust pies on Center Blvd steps from the library orbit.
restaurants.praise: Crust/toppings when the kitchen is on.
restaurants.kid_note: On Center Blvd on the Ridge, a short walk from the Spook-tacular start. Sat 11–9, Sun 11–8:30.

restaurants.name: Saints & Scholars Irish Pub
restaurants.known_for: Irish-pub comfort food (burgers, fish & chips, sausage rolls) in a cozy Ridge spot.
restaurants.praise: Portions, fireside vibe, and attentive service.
restaurants.kid_note: Sat brunch/early dinner; confirm kids’ menu items day-of.

restaurants.name: Sno Thai Café
restaurants.known_for: Family-owned Thai curries, noodles, and desserts on Center Blvd (chef-owned; long family recipes).
restaurants.praise: Pad Thai, crab fried rice, friendly owners, and big portions.
restaurants.kid_note: Sat dinner hours after LEGO — confirm open time day-of; mild noodle plates split well.

restaurants.name: Sigillo Cellars (Snoqualmie)
restaurants.known_for: Family-run winery tasting room in downtown Snoqualmie with a full food menu (salads, flatbreads, shareable plates) and non-alcoholic drinks.
restaurants.kid_note: Kids of any age welcome (they count toward the party size and stay seated with you). No play area. Sat noon–10, Sun noon–5.

restaurants.name: Snoqualmie Ice Cream (Historic Downtown SQ, near SQ Depot)
restaurants.known_for: Local scoop-shop flavors (German Chocolate Cake, Mukilteo Mudd, honey lavender) at 8102 Railroad Ave SE — rebuilt/reopened after the 2024 fire.
restaurants.praise: Rich creamy scoops, friendly service, and shaded outdoor tables.
restaurants.kid_note: Opens around noon on weekends; a costume-friendly treat after the Snoqualmie return.

ideas.name: Trick or Treat at Redmond Town Center
ideas.hook: Free Halloween trick-or-treating at participating shops around the outdoor mall.
ideas.drive: ~30 min via Redmond-Fall City Rd or I-90 W / SR 520
ideas.hours_detail: Sat Oct 31 only, 4–6 PM. 7345 164th Ave NE, Redmond. Treats while supplies last.
ideas.why: An easy after-nap version of Halloween: flat sidewalks, shops close together, and dinner right there. Done by 6 if you'd rather skip the evening neighborhood rounds.
ideas.rain_backup: Outdoor walkways; Saturday afternoon looks dry.

good_to_know.hours_note: Look for the pumpkin decal on participating stores. Treats last while supplies do.

restaurants.name: Postdoc Brewing (Redmond)
restaurants.known_for: Taproom a few blocks from the community center with daily food trucks, non-alcoholic drinks and games.
restaurants.kid_note: Kids allowed ("Bring everyone!"). Sat 11–10; check their calendar for that day's truck.

restaurants.name: Mac & Jack's Brewery (Redmond)
restaurants.known_for: Redmond brewery taproom and beer garden with rotating food trucks.
restaurants.kid_note: Family-friendly beer garden. Hours and the day's truck aren't posted on their site; call (425) 558-9697.

restaurants.name: Spark Pizza
restaurants.known_for: Wood-fired pizza in a converted house near Redmond Town Center, with a covered patio and fire pit.
restaurants.kid_note: Share a pie before or after the trick-or-treat loop.

restaurants.name: Pomegranate Bistro
restaurants.known_for: Southern-leaning American comfort food in a roomy, family-friendly café.
restaurants.praise: Kids’ meals, hash browns, brunch plates, and attentive staff.
restaurants.kid_note: High chairs and roomy tables for a proper sit-down lunch.

restaurants.name: Molly Moon’s Homemade Ice Cream (downtown Redmond)
restaurants.known_for: Scratch-made Seattle scoops, seasonal flavors, and fresh waffle cones in the historic bank building on Cleveland St.
restaurants.praise: Creamy unique flavors (honey lavender, coconut), friendly staff, and generous scoops.
restaurants.kid_note: Near Town Center; expect a line.

ideas.name: Day of the Dead Celebration in Issaquah
ideas.hook: Free Día de los Muertos afternoon focused on Oaxaca: mask decorating, three art workshops, face painting, traditional dancers and mariachi.
ideas.cost: Free; a ticket is needed for each person
ideas.hours_detail: Sun Nov 1 only, 1–5 PM. Issaquah Community Center, 301 Rainier Blvd S.
ideas.why: Something different for Sunday: music, dancing and crafts indoors. It overlaps nap, so go at 3 for the last two hours, then early dinner in downtown Issaquah.

good_to_know.hours_note: Register for free tickets ahead (up to 5 per order; families can place more than one order). Food is sold on site.

restaurants.name: Levitate Gastropub
restaurants.known_for: Scratch-made modern American pub on Front St, open to all ages, with a kids' menu.
restaurants.kid_note: About a 3-minute walk from Front St; easy early dinner after the celebration.

restaurants.name: Formula Brewing
restaurants.known_for: Issaquah brewery with a taproom, beer garden and kitchen (pizza, wings, salads, pretzels).
restaurants.kid_note: Kids welcome inside and out (supervised). Open 11:30 daily; Sat to 10, Sun to 9. About 10 min from the farm.

restaurants.name: Flying Pie Pizzeria
restaurants.known_for: Locally owned pizzeria on Front St in downtown Issaquah.
restaurants.kid_note: Easy shared pies after the creek.

restaurants.name: Boehm’s Candies
restaurants.known_for: Issaquah chocolate and candy maker since 1942: hand-dipped chocolates, caramels and seasonal Halloween treats.
restaurants.kid_note: Sun 10–6. A short drive up Gilman Blvd.

ideas.name: Snoqualmie Falls upper viewpoints
ideas.hook: The 270-foot falls from the upper park's observation decks, a short stroll from the lot, with big spray after rain.
ideas.cost: Free (free lot across the street; paid lot $7/hr)
ideas.hours_detail: Open sunrise to sunset, 365 days a year
ideas.why: The quickest big-wow outing from home: flat paved paths to the overlook, room for the 2-year-old to walk, and a fast exit if moods turn. Sunday afternoon looks sunny, a good easy outing after a big Halloween.

restaurants.kid_note: Short walk from the Snoqualmie Depot; booths and kids' options.

filler_bank: Halloween Harvest Market, Bellevue Farmers Market (Sat Oct 31, 10–3; vendor trick-or-treat, scavenger hunt, face painting)
Little Monsters on Main Street, Old Bellevue (Sat Oct 31, 1–3; free; overlaps nap)
Halloween Factoria, Bellevue (Sat Oct 31, 2–4; free; kids 12 and under in costume)
Great Pumpkin Hunt, Woodinville library (Sat Oct 31, 4–5:30; free; mini pumpkin, small costume parade)
Trick or Treat at the Library, KCLS Bellevue (Sat Oct 31, 11–6; free treat at the Children's Desk)
Día de Muertos at Seattle Center Armory (Sat–Sun 11–6; free; sugar skull and paper flower workshops)
